item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E001","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The Federal Court of Auditors reported 29 federal special funds, including a €100 billion Bundeswehr fund and a €200 billion Economic Stabilization Fund. Larger existing special funds totaled about €869 billion, with roughly €522 billion in debt potential at the end of 2022. It said special funds endangered parliamentary budget rights and the effectiveness of the debt rule, and that federal plans to reduce them were insufficient, particularly regarding the Climate and Transformation Fund.","notes":["Narrowed “weakened” to the excerpt’s wording that the arrangements endangered budget rights and debt-rule effectiveness."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E005","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"In November 2023, Russia withdrew its ratification of the CTBT after parliamentary approval, had suspended participation in New START earlier in the year, and had continued nuclear threats and deployed tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus. The report said Russia intended to continue supplying data from its 32 monitoring stations.","notes":["Replaced the unsupported claim that the monitoring organization continued receiving data with the excerpt’s statement that Russia intended to continue supplying data."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E009","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E010","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E011","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Germany's 2023 disarmament report stated that the federal government continued international responsibility for arms control, disarmament, and non-proliferation; it emphasized risk reduction and avoiding unintended escalation, support for the NPT, preventing Iranian nuclear armament and North Korean nuclear expansion, maintaining chemical- and biological-weapons prohibitions, developing rules for autonomous weapons and space, cybersecurity cooperation, and humanitarian controls on small arms, weapons systems inconsistent with international humanitarian law, and ammunition.","notes":["Replaced “prohibited weapons” with the excerpt’s narrower description: weapons systems inconsistent with international humanitarian law."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E012","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
